required_statement: There exists a proper isosceles triangle whose two base angle measures are each twice its apex angle measure.
proof_spine: Reuse golden-cut parameter t>0, t<1, t^2=1-t from II.11.
Construct A=(0,0), B=(1,0), D=((1+t)/2,sqrt(1-((1+t)/2)^2)); positive height gives a proper triangle.
Squared side lengths are AB^2=AD^2=1 and BD^2=t^2.
Compute apex cosine (1+t)/2 and both base cosines t/2 using existing angle interfaces.
Golden quadratic identity gives cos(2*apex)=t/2; principal ranges establish the actual doubled angle measures.
semantic_boundary: An equal-sided metric certificate or cosine equality alone is not IV.10 completion; actual angle measure doubling and triangle nondegeneracy are required.
